who, which, that: relative-clause marker after a noun (distinct from ti: the perfect marker and 'of')
at, in, on: locative preposition before a noun; also to have, to possess (distinct from ni: the copula and focus marker)
you: second-person singular subject pronoun before the verb; also the sentence-final particle of warmth or emphasis (distinct from ó: he, she, it)
not: negator before the verb, the short form of kò (distinct from ó: he, she, it)
will: future marker before the verb; also him, her, it as the object pronoun echoing a verb whose vowel is a (distinct from a: we)
and then, and so: links a following clause, standing after the subject pronoun (distinct from sí: to, toward)
